walkthroughs.body_html:
Area E: The International World — a core area of GCSE French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area E: The International World brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area E: The International World.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In which year did Algeria gain independence from France?
Which is NOT part of the Maghreb?
options: Algérie
Maroc
Tunisie
Sénégal

mcqs.q: What is the 'vous' form of 'être' in the present tense?
options: When you don't know what tense to use.
êtes.
est.
êtez.

mcqs.q: When do you use the imperfect rather than the passé composé?
options: For ongoing, habitual, or descriptive past actions.
Adding 'pas' at the end.
Just for older events.
When you don't know what tense to use.

mcqs.q: What is the most common informal way to form a yes/no question in French?
options: Adding 'pas' at the end.
Rising intonation (statement said as a question) or using 'est-ce que'.
Always using inversion (Parlez-vous?).
est.
